item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Fri Oct 30, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: How to Catch a Turkey STEM Activity — Mon Nov 23, 3:00 PM — Eastern Lancaster County
item.description:
STEM, Children, Tweens
Join us for a festive, hands-on maker workshop inspired by Adam Wallace’s bestselling children's book, How to Catch a Turkey. Kids will step into the shoes of real structural engineers to design, build, and test their very own turkey traps using everyday building materials. Recommended for ages 8-12! Registration is required!🛠️ The Engineering MissionThe Story Setup: We will start with a reading of How to Catch a Turkey to study the turkey's clever escape tactics.The Blueprint: Kids will brainstorm, sketch, and map out their trap concepts on official design sheets.The Construction: Makers will use their engineering supplies to bring their structures to life.The Field Test: We will wrap up the program by testing every trap to see if it can successfully a paper turkey!
Source: Lancaster Libraries
